stem: Which pair of age ranges matches the usual age pattern for type 1 diabetes diagnosis in childhood?
explanation: 4-6 years and 10-14 years is the correct age pattern for type 1 diabetes diagnosis in childhood.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes in Children and Adolescents Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because infancy and 2-3 years are not the age bands described for the usual diagnosis pattern.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because type 1 diabetes in children is typically diagnosed in two peaks, at 4-6 years and 10-14 years.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 7-9 years and 15-17 years are not the age ranges given for the usual pattern.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the pattern is not described as spanning from birth to 18 years; it has two typical age peaks.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 1-2 years and 12-16 years do not match the age ranges stated in the usual pattern.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
